chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Khatli, from Ahmad ibn Idris al-Qummi, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Kufi, from al-Abbas ibn A'mir, from Sayf ibn Umayra, from al-Jarud ibn al-Mundhir, from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
No Hashimite woman among us combed her hair or applied dye [to it] – until al-Mukhtar sent to us the heads of those who killed al-Husayn (peace be upon him).

key_terms.اختضبت: Applied henna or dye (a grooming ritual)

ai.seo_question: What did the Hashimite women do while waiting for news of Imam al-Husayn's martyrdom?
ai.summary: This hadith from Rijal al-Kashshi highlights the profound grief of the Hashimite women during the interregnum between Imam al-Husayn's martyrdom and the arrival of his killers' heads via al-Mukhtar ibn Abi Ubayda. Their abstention from grooming (combining hair and applying henna) serves as a traditional sign of mourning, illustrating the deep emotional impact of the event on the Ahl al-Bayt's household before the news of vengeance was confirmed.
